title: The Lighter Brief
overview: This edition is a mixed bag with a few bright spots. Guyana hit a major health milestone, Charlotte neighbors won a fight over some protected dogwood trees, and Becky G is heading into an independent new chapter. There's also a gentle goodbye to Fiona the hippo, plus some practical Thanksgiving travel notes and a couple of policy and health-system updates.

stories.headline: Stomach bug sweeps a Princess cruise ship
stories.summary: Nearly 150 people aboard a Princess cruise ship on a 12-night Caribbean trip came down with vomiting and diarrhea from an illness that hasn't been identified yet. The cruise line is cleaning more, isolating sick passengers and collecting samples for testing.
key_facts: 148 people affected, according to the CDC
Symptoms were reported on day five of the trip
It's the 10th cruise outbreak reported this year
The CDC counts it as an outbreak when 3% or more of passengers get sick
disputed: The cause of the illness is still unknown and testing is underway
The cruise industry group says stomach illness is rarer at sea than on land, but that group is funded by the industry
stories.why: If you're cruising soon, frequent handwashing and finding the ship's clinic before you need it are easy ways to stay well.

stories.headline: Goodbye, Fiona: the Cincinnati Zoo's famous hippo has died
stories.summary: Fiona, the hippo who was born premature in 2017 and became a global social media star, died Thursday from complications after swallowing a knit hat. A ceiling fan accidentally flung the hat into her enclosure. Her care team spent more than a week trying to help her, even borrowing a vibration plate from a horse farm and offering her a sniff of coffee, a scent she always liked.
key_facts: Fiona weighed just 29 lbs (13 kg) at birth, about half the lowest previously recorded for her species
She reached 1,000 lbs in 2018
The zoo said the hat getting into her enclosure was an accident
Specialists said surgery wasn't an option for a full-grown hippo
stories.why: Fiona's comeback story charmed millions, and her keepers cared for her devotedly right to the end.

stories.headline: Charlotte billboard ordered removed after protected dogwoods were cut down
stories.summary: North Carolina's Department of Transportation has ordered Adams Outdoor Advertising to take down a Plaza Midwood billboard. Inspectors found the company illegally cut protected dogwood trees while clearing land around the sign. State law now allows clearing within 500 feet of billboards, but dogwoods are an exception. Locals, the group Sustain Charlotte and State Sen. Caleb Theodros pushed for the inspection.
key_facts: Adams has 60 days to remove the billboard but can appeal
40 other permits in Mecklenburg County allow similar clearing
The billboard is near Independence Boulevard and Commonwealth Avenue
Adams said it hadn't been notified yet and would fix any damage if the work was done wrong
stories.why: It shows how neighbors speaking up can make a difference, and local business owners are now hoping for replanting.

stories.headline: Charlotte airport is back to normal and gearing up for 2 million Thanksgiving travelers
stories.summary: After last week's nationwide ground stop caused about 30% of flights to be canceled for two days, Charlotte Douglas says operations are back to normal. Officials expect nearly 2 million travelers over the 13-day holiday period and don't expect more widespread disruptions.
key_facts: The travel period runs Nov. 19 through Dec. 1
More than 9,300 departing flights are scheduled, up 2.6% from last year
The busiest days are expected to be Nov. 28-30
Most parking must be booked in advance
stories.why: If you're flying through CLT, arrive early, book parking ahead and check wait times on the airport's app.

stories.headline: White House replaces its national cyber director
stories.summary: National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was fired, a source close to the White House told AFP. The move follows major outages that disrupted travel, communications and online shopping, along with growing concerns about AI threats. Defense Department CIO Kirsten Davies will fill the role in an acting capacity.
key_facts: According to the source, President Trump backed the firing over Cairncross's credentials
Davies is already Senate-confirmed
Secretary of State Marco Rubio publicly congratulated Davies
stories.why: This office helps protect the systems behind everyday things like travel and online shopping.

stories.headline: Guyana reaches a big milestone for moms and babies
stories.summary: The World Health Organization has confirmed that Guyana has eliminated mother-to-child transmission of HIV and syphilis as public health problems. That puts the country in a select group in Latin America and the Caribbean. The health ministry credited years of investment in screening, treatment, lab services and healthcare workers.
key_facts: The validation covers the period 2022-2025
WHO's advisory committee reviewed Guyana's case on November 5
Guyana will be reviewed again in 2030
disputed: This means transmission is down to elimination levels, not that either infection has been completely eradicated
stories.why: In the health minister's words, it means infections prevented and children given a healthier start in life.

stories.headline: Vinicius Jr. hopes his Brazil scoring spree carries over to Real Madrid
stories.summary: Real Madrid winger Vinicius Junior is back from a four-match ban and could play Saturday against Celta Vigo. He has struggled at club level this season, with just one Madrid goal, but he scored five times in two friendlies for Brazil. He admitted he trained less after Brazil's early World Cup exit.
key_facts: Madrid trail La Liga leaders Barcelona by three points
Vinicius's contract runs until 2032
New signing Yan Diomande has four goals in his last eight games
stories.why: It's a refreshingly candid comeback story: "I'm human, I make mistakes often, but I always try to improve."

links.title: Vinicius ready for Real Madrid battle after Brazil revival

stories.headline: FDA approves a new four-times-a-year treatment for myasthenia gravis
stories.summary: The FDA approved Regeneron's Livsayis (cemdisiran) for adults with the most common form of generalized myasthenia gravis, a neuromuscular disease. It's the second new treatment for the condition approved this week, after AstraZeneca's Klygefa.
key_facts: It's given as an injection just four times a year
It's the first siRNA therapy for the condition and was developed with Alnylam
In its late-stage trial, patients improved by 2.3 points on a daily-living scale compared with placebo
It's Regeneron's first neurology approval
disputed: The drug is fully FDA approved for adults who are anti-AChR antibody-positive
A healthcare provider has to give the shots, which analysts say limits convenience
stories.why: Patients now have more options, including some that require fewer treatments.
